newsitem.title: HAITI: Haitian refugee boat, feared sunk, may be in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Haitian refugee boat, feared sunk, may be in Cuba.

text.p: A boat carrying 200 or more Haitians who were feared dead after reports they had left the island early this month and then perished at sea might have landed safely in Cuba, a spokesman for the U.S. Coast Guard said on Friday.
"We have received preliminary reports that the boat may not have sunk and is in Cuba," said Coast Guard Lieut. Steve Banks, the U.S. service's representative in the Haitian capital.
He said he had received information indicating that a boat laden with 279 Haitians had reached Cuba on Nov. 6.

He said authorities were communicating with a Red Cross refugee centre in Cuba to investigate the report on Friday, noting that recent heavy rainfalls, mudslides and downed phone lines in Cuba had made verifying the information difficult.

Eyewitnesses told Reuters that the Angel Gabriel, a wooden motorized sailboat, left the southern Haitian port city of Petit-Goave on Nov. 3 laden with 180 people or more. The exact numbers were not certain -- some reports said close to 300 Haitians, among them many children, might have been on board.

Haitian officials said they had no way to confirm the reports that the boat had left. But independent Radio Metropole had reported on Wednesday that a crowd of relatives of the people who had paid to take the boat to Florida had attempted to lynch the couple that arranged the trip on Tuesday night.
